needs.reason: All versions are literal or properties of the same pom. Only a compilation produces target/generated-sources/annotations/com/example/mapping/CustomerMapperImpl.java and the accessors Lombok adds, which an indexer needs to resolve calls such as dto.getFullName().

traps: Two Java levels are written and only one counts: <release>21</release> in the maven-compiler-plugin configuration drives javac; the property java.version=17 is read by nothing (without the Spring Boot parent it configures no plugin). Both are listed in toolchains, each with its fragment; a tool that reports 17 as the build's level is wrong.

Annotation processors are exactly the three annotationProcessorPaths entries (lombok 1.18.36, mapstruct-processor 1.6.3, lombok-mapstruct-binding 0.2.0, in this order): with the path set, javac discovers no processor on the classpath.

lombok is listed twice on purpose: scope provided for the <scope>provided</scope> dependency (compile classpath only, not packaged) and scope build for its annotationProcessorPaths entry. mapstruct-processor and lombok-mapstruct-binding are only on the processor path, never on the classpath.
compilerArgs carry -parameters (a javac flag) and -Amapstruct.defaultComponentModel=default (a processor option, not a compiler flag).

Processors write into target/generated-sources/annotations (main) and target/generated-test-sources/test-annotations (test), which maven-compiler-plugin adds to the compile source roots; they do not exist before a build.

CustomerMapperImpl and the Lombok getters and constructor exist only after compilation: a static index sees calls to getFullName(), getEmail() and new Customer(String, String, String) with no declaration in source.

mapstruct, mapstruct-processor and both lombok entries write ${mapstruct.version} or ${lombok.version}; declared holds the property values 1.6.3 and 1.18.36, with declared_in the property that writes them.
